summary_en: Inaba to acquire 100% of Fujikura Shoji (currently Fujikura subsidiary). Target: electronics components and wire/cable distributor, FY3/26 operating profit ¥1,864M, net profit ¥1,295M. Synergy: combine Fujikura product range with Inaba sales network to strengthen proposal capabilities and expand revenue in industrial equipment electronics segment.
title_en: Notice regarding acquisition of shares of Fujikura Shoji Co., Ltd. (complete subsidiary acquisition)
translation_en_brief: On 31 August 2026, Inaba Denki Sangyo (ticker 9934, TSE Prime) announced the Board's decision to acquire all shares of Fujikura Shoji Co., Ltd. (currently a wholly owned subsidiary of Fujikura Co., Ltd.) and make it a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Inaba. Fujikura Shoji's own subsidiary, Fujikura Shoji Trading (Dalian) Limited, will become a grandchild company of Inaba upon completion. Fujikura Shoji, established in 1947, is an electronics components and wire/cable distributor with capital of ¥301M; it serves as Fujikura's domestic sales arm for a broad range of Fujikura group products. For FY3/26, Fujikura Shoji reported standalone operating profit of ¥1,864M and net profit of ¥1,295M on sales of ¥34,490M; combined with its subsidiary (on simple-sum basis), the group posted operating profit of ¥1,895M and net profit of ¥1,314M on sales of ¥35,587M. Inaba's rationale centres on middle-to-long-term strategy to expand its electronics business within the industrial equipment segment; the acquisition is designed to widen the product-range offered, combine Fujikura Shoji's expertise in electronics components and connectors with Inaba's sales network and customer base, thereby strengthen proposal capabilities and revenue opportunity, and accelerate the broader portfolio and enterprise value strategy. Acquisition price, share count, and settlement date are not disclosed in the announcement.
